note: Field values follow WheelView report Table 1 (device_type adds 'unclear', kept out of classification splits per Section 5). Single source of truth for UI, server validation and derivation. v4: chair_subtype=negative_camber. v5: adds securement_hardware (docking_bracket / tiedown_points / not_visible / unclear) — label only what is visible; not a safety certification. v6: retires lighting, environment, weather, ground_wet, size_class, ramp_deploy, ramp_reasons (kept only as retired_fields for reading historical events). Adds device_use_case above device_type.
value_aliases_note: Historical values kept in the append-only event log, mapped to the canonical option on read (wvcore.canon). 'lookalike' was renamed 'ambiguous' on 2026-10-28; old events are never rewritten. Prefill keys (lookalike_*) are candidate source categories from data/candidates.csv, not label values.

extra_fields.exclude: one of exclude_reasons or '' (= not excluded); compared between annotators
extra_fields.bbox: JSON list of [x,y,w,h] in 0..1 image coordinates, or []; not compared, kept per annotator
extra_fields._status: 'done' when the annotator has finished the image; only 'done' annotators count towards consensus
extra_fields._status_v11: 'done' when the annotator has finished the v1.1 attribute pass on the image (independent of _status)

note_v11: v1.1 fields ("since": "1.1") are labelled in the Attributes pass (own done flag _status_v11). Schema v6: the Attributes section also shows and lets any labeler edit the latest saved core labels (device_use_case, device_type, occupied, etc.); edits append correction events, never rewrite history. device_use_case is optional on already-labelled images (unset = not yet labelled) and required on new saves. They never change v1.0 release artifacts or frozen v1.0 splits. Unlabelled (no event) is different from 'unknown'. Definitions: server/schema.json definitions and docs/DATA_DICTIONARY_v1.1.md.

control.joystick: a powered-chair joystick / hand control is visible (usually on an armrest)
control.attendant_control: a rear/attendant joystick or the push handles are being used by a second person to steer the device
control.push_rims: hand rims on the large wheels are visible and are the user's means of propulsion (manual chair, no attendant steering)
control.tiller: handlebar tiller steering of a mobility scooter
control.none_visible: the device's control is not in view or the device has none (e.g. walker, ambiguous look-alike)
control.unknown: cannot be determined from the photo

environment.sidewalk: pedestrian sidewalk / footpath away from the curb edge
environment.curbside: at the curb edge or curb ramp, i.e. the boarding/alighting position next to the roadway
environment.crosswalk_road: in a crosswalk or on the roadway itself
environment.vehicle_interior: inside a car, van, bus or train
environment.ramp_lift: on a vehicle ramp or lift, or a building ramp used for boarding
environment.other_outdoor: any other outdoor place (park, beach, sports court, trail, plain studio background)
environment.unknown: cannot be determined from the photo

environment_from_v10_setting._note: used ONLY as an (unconfirmed) suggestion in the attribute pass; never written as a label

weather.sunny_clear: outdoor, direct sun or clear sky
weather.overcast: outdoor, cloudy / diffuse light, no precipitation visible
weather.rain: rain visible (falling drops, umbrellas in use, rain gear)
weather.snow: falling snow or snow on the ground
weather.night: outdoor at night (weather otherwise not judgeable)
weather.indoor_na: indoor or vehicle interior: weather not applicable
weather.unknown: outdoor but weather cannot be judged (e.g. tight crop)

ground_wet.yes: visibly wet / puddles / snow-slush on the ground
ground_wet.unknown: ground not visible or cannot be judged

size_class.standard: device looks like a typical adult chair width
size_class.wide: device is visibly wider than a typical chair (e.g. bariatric-width or large power base) relative to the user/surroundings
size_class.unknown: cannot be judged (occluded, no reference, not a chair)
size_class._note: a coarse VISUAL judgement only, never a measurement; metric sizes only come from data/measurements.csv
size_class.pediatric_size: the device itself is visibly child-sized (small frame). A SIZE DESCRIPTOR ONLY: images showing a child are excluded (exclude=child) and never labelled, so this applies to empty or adult-occupied small chairs

chair_subtype.standard_folding: manual: standard folding (cross-brace) frame, usually with swing-away footrests and push handles
chair_subtype.lightweight_rigid: manual: lightweight rigid / sport / active-user frame (fixed frame, often cambered wheels, low back, no or small push handles)
chair_subtype.negative_camber: manual: negative camber (wheels angled in at the top / out at the ground; sports/active chairs ? distinct from a plain lightweight_rigid frame)
chair_subtype.transport_attendant: manual: transport / attendant-propelled chair (small rear wheels, no push rims; pushed by a second person)
chair_subtype.tilt_recline: manual: tilt-in-space or reclining chair (large padded seat and headrest, tilt mechanism)
chair_subtype.power_standard: powered: standard power chair (power base, joystick, fixed seat)
chair_subtype.power_tilt_recline: powered: power tilt / recline / elevating seating functions visible (actuators, tilted seat, headrest)
chair_subtype.unknown: cannot tell the subtype from the photo
chair_subtype._note: dependent on device_type: manual subtypes when device_type is manual; powered subtypes when powered. Scooters stay device_type=other_aid (no subtype). Pediatric is not a subtype (child images are excluded).

drive_position.mid_wheel: powered: drive wheels in the middle of the base (6-wheel look, small casters front and rear)
drive_position.front_wheel: powered: large drive wheels at the front
drive_position.rear_wheel: powered: large drive wheels at the back
drive_position.unknown: drive wheels not visible or cannot tell

ramp_deploy.safe: in this image, a vehicle ramp/lift could be deployed here and used safely: space, flat enough surface, no obstruction and a wheelchair user waiting to board
ramp_deploy.unsafe: a ramp should NOT be deployed here now: give the reasons
ramp_deploy.not_needed: no ramp is needed (e.g. nobody in a wheelchair waiting, or the user is not trying to board): give the reasons
ramp_deploy._note: an image-level RESEARCH judgement by the annotator, not a safety assessment, not validated for deployment decisions

ramp_reasons.insufficient_space: not enough clear space for the ramp and the turning chair
ramp_reasons.obstruction: pole, bin, parked car, bollard, people or objects in the way
ramp_reasons.curb_height_issue: curb too high/low or no curb where needed
ramp_reasons.traffic_hazard: moving traffic or bike lane in the ramp area
ramp_reasons.user_not_waiting_unclear: a user is present but not waiting to board, or intent is unclear
ramp_reasons._note: multi-select, recorded only when ramp_deploy is unsafe or not_needed. Stored as a JSON list; derived files join the sorted values with '+'

securement_hardware.docking_bracket: a docking pin/bracket under the seat is clearly visible (e.g. EZ Lock / Q'Straint-style docking hardware)
securement_hardware.tiedown_points: marked securement loops or brackets for 4-point tiedowns are clearly visible (WC19-style)
securement_hardware.not_visible: the photo shows a wheelchair/mobility device but no docking or tiedown hardware is in view
securement_hardware.unclear: cannot tell from this photo whether securement hardware is present (too small, occluded, or ambiguous)
securement_hardware._annotator_rule: Label only what is visible. Do not infer hardware from chair brand alone. Prefer unclear over guessing.
securement_hardware._vehicle_guidance: docking_bracket at high model confidence may INFORM preparing a docking station for boarding; not_visible, unclear, or low confidence => defer to rider confirmation. This field is NOT a safety certification and must never alone authorize securement or boarding.

device_use_case.specialized: the device is for a more special use case (e.g. sports, racing, heavy-duty / bariatric, pediatric-sized, rehab / tilt-recline complex seating) rather than everyday community use
device_use_case.standard: the device looks like an everyday / general-purpose mobility aid (typical manual or power chair, walker, scooter for daily use)
device_use_case.unknown: cannot reasonably tell the use case from the photo
device_use_case._note: a coarse visual judgement of intended use, not a clinical classification; unset (no event) means not yet labelled

measurement_note: Schema v6: size estimates and tape-measured dimensions are retired from the annotator, label filter, derive/export, and training-split manifests. Existing data/measurements.csv and scripts/size_estimate.py outputs are not deleted, but they are not exported into new training manifests. Historical size_class / ramp / weather / lighting / environment / ground_wet events stay in the append-only log and are ignored on derive.
changelog_v6: Schema v6 (2026-11-09): retire lighting (v1.0), environment, weather, ground_wet, size_class, ramp_deploy, and ramp_reasons from the annotator, validation of new events, label filter, derive/export, and training-split manifests. Historical events in annotations/events/*.jsonl are never rewritten; derive/export ignore those keys. Add device_use_case (specialized / standard / unknown) above device_type. v1.0 release artifacts stay frozen.
retired_note: retired_fields lists schema v6 removals. Readers may accept historical values (validate(..., allow_retired=True)); new writes are rejected. Fold/export/filter ignore them.
